chapter_title: The Descent and the Encounter with Ella
summary: Joe explores the limitations of Jory's constructed world and realizes that it extends only a few blocks. He encounters a blond girl who reveals herself to be Ella Runciter, Glen's wife, who is in half-life but able to operate autonomously against Jory. Ella explains that she is deteriorating and will soon be reborn, and that she has been helping Joe because she wants him to become Glen's advisor in half-life after her departure. She gives Joe a certificate guaranteeing him a lifetime supply of Ubik. Ella and Joe go to a drugstore, but Jory has regressed the Ubik there into a nineteenth-century liver balm. Joe, with great effort, attempts to consciously evolve the balm back to a spray can, and a factory representative appears with the needed Ubik. The chapter establishes that there are forces within half-life working to counteract Jory, and that human will and consciousness can actually reshape the pseudo-world.

themes: The power of will and consciousness over material reality
The renewal of hope and purpose
Responsibility passed to the next generation

theological_concepts.concept: Angels and guides in the afterlife
Divine grace manifested through human agency
The communion of souls across the boundary of life and death

philosophical_concepts.concept: Idealism: the power of consciousness to shape reality
Teleology and purpose in the afterlife
The relationship between will, effort, and manifestation
